flags: Suspected error (copied unchanged), mud: the card has lūtum, lūtī n. Lewis & Short has lŭtum (short u) “mud, mire” (Cic. Verr. 2.4.53; Caes. B.C. 2.15), while lūtum (long u) is weld, the yellow dye plant (Verg. E. 4.44). Probably lutum, lutī n.
Suspected error (copied unchanged), share: the card has communicō, communicāre; Lewis & Short prints commūnĭco, from commūnis. Probably commūnicō, commūnicāre.
Suspected error (copied unchanged), seesaw: the card has tollenō, tollenōnis m.; Lewis & Short prints tollēno, ōnis (long e).

Suspected error (copied unchanged), climbing hold, handhold, foothold: ansa, ansae f. (and ansam, ansae in the examples). Lewis & Short leaves the a unmarked, but a vowel before ns is long (Bennett; Allen, Vox Latina), and the lexicon itself writes ōlla ānsāta (saucepan). Probably ānsa, ānsae f.

ēsca (bait): the card calls it “the series spelling” without saying what it departs from; Lewis & Short prints esca. The latinitas standards cite de Vaan s.v. edō (Jack, 31 Oct). A note, and perhaps a ruling, may be wanted; none was invented.

mīlvus (kite): Lewis & Short prints miluus unmarked; the card’s long i agrees with verse (trisyllabic mīluus in a fifth-foot dactyl, Hor. Ep. 1.16.51), so it is not flagged as an error, but the card gives no note.

Recommended forms to review. Slide: the card leads with Morgan–Owens’s tractus lūbricus; the libellī use tabula dēclīvis (alternative here). Playground: ārea lūsōria (card lead, Traupman) recommended; the family word lūsōrium (Libellus VII) is an alternative. Football (the game): pedifollium (Traupman 47, “the word Libellus VII uses”) recommended over the card’s older first form pilā pedibus lūdere.

Recommended forms to review. Violin: the card bolds Lewis & Short’s plural fidiculae, fidiculārum f. while discussing Traupman’s fidicula; Traupman’s fidicula (the form given for violin) is recommended, the plural is in its comment, and Morgan–Owens’s violīnum is an alternative. Draughts: Traupman’s latrunculī leads, as on the card, though the card notes that Morgan–Owens uses latrunculī for chess and the Roman latrunculī was a third game; lūdus damicus may be clearer. Amusement park: Traupman’s oblectāriī leads although oblectārius is not in Lewis & Short. Ice skates: patinī leads (card order) though coined on Italian.

Periods where the card is silent, from Lewis & Short: fābula scaenica post-classical (Amm. 28.1.4); scaenica “actress” late (Cod. Just.; Ambrose); praestigiārī modern (Lewis & Short has praestigior only from the Glossae Cyrilli); oscillō post-classical (Festus); neurospaston post-classical (Gellius); circulus “hoop” classical (Verg., Plin., Suet.); per vicēs classical (Ov. M. 4.40); grūs as a machine classical (Vitr. 10.19); petaurista classical (Varro, Lucilius). Shuffle and deal are renaissance: Morgan–Owens’s entries cite Vives 1540 (checked in latinitas refs/morgan-owens-adumbratio.txt).

Periods chosen as the later one because the card neither labels nor cites them: ours for ferrum trānsversum, harēnāria (sandpit), pede pulsāre, pedibus pellere, stāns lābī, ūnā lūdere and Fēcī!; modern for piscātum īre (cited only to Traupman) and for lūdibrium “toy” (the card cites Traupman for the neutral toy sense; classical if “plaything” counts). Minimum āfuit quīn facerēs! is classical by its idiom (Suet. Aug. 14, Caes. B.C. 2.35); the sentence itself is composed.

The Seneca line is cited on the card as “Sen. Ben. II 17, 4; quoted in Libellus VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae”. check_libelli reads only a bare Libellus source, so the example cites Seneca and the lūsor comment says it is quoted in Libellus VII.

Card markup, gone with the conversion: several cards mark English labels as Latin (violin:, piano:, take a photo:, cinema:, ice skates:, playing card:, chess:, draughts, checkers:) and mark Italian pattinare as Latin; the record gives pattinare as Italian, in <em>.

Whistle: the card says neither source has a settled word for the toy whistle, but Traupman’s English–Latin list gives fistula (pipe) and fistulā sībilāre for blowing a whistle (latinitas refs/traupman-conversational-latin.txt). Not added.

Domain kept as ludi, though these plainly belong elsewhere: together, again, enough, wait, share, lend, give back (sermo); sand, gravel, grass, ground, mud, puddle, shade, sunshine (natura or aedificatio); bench, fence, gate (urbs or domus-structura); rope, knot, strap (officina); tractor, excavator, bulldozer, truck, dump truck, crane, trailer, loader, wheelbarrow (aedificatio or vectura); camera, photo, take a photo, television, television set, remote control, radio (domus or computatra).

Likely overlaps with unconverted cards in other categories (same headword and sense, so a merge will need one record): entry-75 play, game, ball, doll, toy bear; entry-78 wait, take turns; entry-6 and entry-93 jump, hop; entry-94 hang, hold on; entry-287 climb, go down, top; entry-288 hold on, let go, push, pull; entry-290 euge, again; entry-28 mud, puddle; entry-27 ground; entry-148 bucket; entry-284 sieve; entry-266 dig; entry-125 and entry-85 fill, pour; entry-131 share; entry-219 truck (autoraeda onerāria); entry-151 sand; entry-162 gravel; entry-195 sand pit; entry-173 crossbar; entry-203 grass; entry-62 knot; entry-196 jog (tolūtim cursitāre) and slowly; entry-221 tunnel; entry-229 bell. The existing colander record lists “sieve” in also.
No card in this batch repeats the twelve swimming records, so none was extended.
Personal names kept to the examples: “with Theo” in the lūsōrium comment and the two climbing source notes reads “with the child”, and the glide comment “As in Libellus VII”.
